question: Should OpenClaw expose a configurable exec approval timeout, and if so what public key, precedence, maximum, and fail-closed semantics should it use?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing config surface, but choosing a public host-exec authorization window is a product and security-boundary decision that automation should not make alone.

options.title: Define a bounded timeout contract
options.body: Add one maintainer-approved key with conservative bounds and thread it through every approval registration, wait, docs, and validation surface.

options.title: Keep the fixed default
options.body: Leave the 30-minute timeout as the only supported behavior and close configurability requests as not planned.

options.title: Prefer UX and fail-fast fixes
options.body: Improve notices, recovery, and no-route fail-fast behavior without adding a new timeout configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded timeout contract
recommendation.body: Add one maintainer-approved key with conservative bounds and thread it through every approval registration, wait, docs, and validation surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The history and prior review context route the timeout/config API decision through steipete's work on the shared exec approval timeout and related reviews.
